metadata.title: Coconut | Convexity evaluation
metadata.description: Evaluate how a language model classifies scalar functions on exact intervals. Inspect reference evidence, three fresh trials, and every reported score.

shared.footer: Model evaluations over explicit mathematical domains

hero.title: Test a model’s convexity judgment
hero.description: Give a language model a function and an exact interval. Compare its answer with a verified reference, then inspect the evidence behind the score.
hero.keyNotice: Use your own provider key. Provider charges apply.

illustration.label: Illustrative function

graph.accessibilityTitle: A convex curve on the closed interval from minus one to one
graph.accessibilityDescription: The natural logarithm of one plus the exponential of x squared sits below a dashed chord joining x equals minus 0.8 and 0.8. Its second derivative is positive throughout the interval. The drawing illustrates the chord condition; one pictured chord alone is not a global proof.

illustration.caption: Illustration only, separate from evaluated suites. Natural log; the second derivative is positive throughout the interval.

task.title: Classify the whole interval
task.description: A function can be convex on one interval and neither on another. The task asks for convex, concave or neither on exactly the domain supplied.
task.exclusionNote: Affine and constant functions satisfy both curvature definitions and are excluded from this three-label task.

examples.title: Illustrative examples
examples.chordExplanation: For every x, y ∈ D and t ∈ [0, 1], set z = tx + (1 − t)y. The chord height at z is t f(x) + (1 − t)f(y).

cards.title: Convex
cards.definition: A convex function is a real-valued function whose graph curves upward like a cup (∪).
cards.reason: For x², f″(x) = 2 > 0 throughout D, so it is convex.

graph.accessibilityDescription: Graph of x squared on [−1, 1]. The curve lies below the dashed chord joining (−1, 1) and (1, 1).

cards.title: Concave
cards.definition: A concave function is a real-valued function whose graph curves downward like an upside-down cup (∩).
cards.reason: For −x², f″(x) = −2 < 0 throughout D, so it is concave.

graph.accessibilityDescription: Graph of minus x squared on [−1, 1]. The curve lies above the dashed chord joining (−1, −1) and (1, −1).

cards.title: Neither
cards.definition: Both definitions fail on D: the graph is above its left chord and below its right chord.
cards.reason: For x³, f″(x) = 6x is negative on (−1, 0) and positive on (0, 1), so it is neither on D.

graph.accessibilityDescription: Graph of x cubed on [−1, 1]. The curve lies above the chord from (−1, −1) to (0, 0), violating convexity, and below the chord from (0, 0) to (1, 1), violating concavity.

examples.note: Cup shapes describe the bend. A convex function can keep increasing or decreasing throughout the interval; it does not need a turning point. Solid lines show functions; dashed lines show selected chords. The derivative checks establish the labels on the whole interval. These examples are separate from the tasks used to score models.

workflow.title: From a function to an inspectable result
workflow.description: The curvature challenge contains 72 certified tasks across eight function families and 24 related parameter groups. Three trials per task make 216 planned requests.

steps.title: Choose your model
steps.description: Select a provider, model, suite and answer format. Review the planned requests and approve your provider’s charges.

steps.title: Run three fresh trials
steps.description: Each request receives one function and its exact interval. Reference labels and verification evidence stay outside the model prompt.

steps.title: Inspect each answer
steps.description: Read returned text beside its reference evidence. Explore macro-F1, accuracy, class detail and the work that remains incomplete.

workflow.depthNote: Depth describes the expression tree. It also changes with function family and size, so a depth plot does not isolate mathematical difficulty.

privacyAndAccess.title: Your key and your run
paragraphs: Your provider key is held in current-page memory and passed through the evaluation server for your requested operation. It is excluded from saved runs. Results are private by default, expire after seven days and use a separate access code.
Save that access code to return to a record. Publication is explicit and reversible. Interrupted work does not resume automatically; requests already sent may still incur provider charges.

comparisons.title: Compare with the settings in view
paragraphs: Suite membership, answer format, reasoning effort and output ceiling define a comparison. Inspect incomplete work and format failures alongside the score. A result on these tasks does not establish general mathematical ability.
OpenAI has live execution checks. OpenRouter and Hugging Face Inference Providers have passed controlled software tests; their live execution remains unverified.
